quote: We demonstrate that interference in multilingual translation largely occurs when the model is very small compared to the abundance of training data, and that the simple principled approach of enlarging the model and tuning the data sampling temperature provides a consistent solution to the interference problem that can even promote synergy.

We define interference as a negative interaction between different translation directions ... measured by the relative difference in performance (test-set cross-entropy loss) between a bilingual model ... and a multilingual counterpart ... We also provide the test BLEU scores achieved by our models.

We assume a common multilingual translation setup that involves L language pairs s → t, where the source is always the same language s (English), and the target language t varies (English-to-many), or vice versa (many-to-English).
datasets: WMT-based benchmark of Siddhant et al. (2020)

quote: We use SacreBLEU to calculate test sets BLEU scores.
